What Zelda analyzed The work behind this report — counted, not estimated. 12 Pages analyzed 12 Sections searched 2 Categories analyzed Business Model & Growth Analysis Insufficient disclosed data to describe the business model. No revenue model, pricing structure, customer type, or growth mechanism was extracted from the document. The only indicators of commercial activity are the company's self-reported traction figures — 140,000+ bots [S1] and 500M messages or 500M messages/month (see consistency note below) [S2, S3] — contextualised under a slide heading 'Traction by Apr-16', but these figures are undated as counts and have not been independently verified [C2, C3, C4]. How the company monetises these users, what drives bot creation, and what the expansion strategy is are not found in the extracted evidence. Information Readiness Score: 10/100 Present: • Self-reported funding total from Pitch Deck Hunt: $23.1M [S4] • Self-reported traction metrics: 140,000+ bots and 500M messages, contextualised to a slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16' [S1, S2] • Self-reported usage rate on a separate slide: 500M messages/month [S3] • Profile-level stage (Series A) and sector (Software) [P1, P2] Needs Validation: • Funding amount and round history (checked but unconfirmed) [C1] • Bot count and message volume metrics (checked but unconfirmed) [C2, C3, C4] • Clarification of whether 500M messages is a cumulative total or a monthly rate [C2, C3] • Revenue, burn, gross margin, and unit economics • Team identities and credentials • Product description and feature set • Market size and competitive landscape • Business model and pricing • Problem statement and target customer • Use of proceeds Next evidence to supply: Audited or accountant-reviewed financials showing revenue, gross margin, and monthly burn rate, together with a clear definition of how the 500M messages figure is measured (cumulative vs. monthly). Supported Points Pitch Deck Hunt lists $23.1M raised [S4], indicating the company has attracted external capital, though the figure is undated and unverified [C1]. The company states 140,000+ bots and 500M messages under a slide headed 'Traction by Apr-16' [S1, S2], suggesting meaningful platform activity at that point, subject to the caveat that neither figure has been independently confirmed [C3, C4]. Open Concerns The 500M messages figure appears twice with different measurement bases — as an undated total on page 10 and as a monthly rate on page 12 [C2, C3] — and the two cannot be compared or confirmed as equivalent without clarification; this ambiguity goes to the reliability of the company's own traction reporting. No revenue, burn, or use-of-proceeds information was extracted, leaving the economic viability of the business entirely uncharacterised. No team information was extracted, making it impossible to assess whether the people building and selling the product have relevant domain experience or a track record. The $23.1M funding figure, reported by Pitch Deck Hunt [S4], is undated and was checked but could not be independently confirmed [C1], leaving the company's capitalisation history unverified. What Would Change the Picture The single most important missing piece is a dated income statement or management accounts showing revenue, gross margin, and monthly cash burn — this would allow an assessment of whether the stated message and bot volumes translate into any economic activity, and would anchor the funding and runway picture that is currently absent from the extracted evidence.
